subject.title: [Bug]: Kimi Coding auth fallback in systemd Gateway when config env is not injected

question: For systemd-managed Gateway turns, should root config env provider keys be treated as durable runtime credentials, service-managed environment entries, or CLI/status-only diagnostics?
rationale: The code already applies config env during config snapshot reads, while the generated service environment intentionally avoids embedding literal config env values; choosing the wrong fix can either leave Kimi turns failing or change credential storage semantics for existing services.

options.title: Keep config-env runtime support
options.body: Confirm config env is supported for managed Gateway turns, add live/systemd proof plus tests, and make `models status` reflect the same runtime context.

options.title: Move users to auth profiles
options.body: Declare config env as setup/config-only for managed services, update Kimi docs/status wording, and steer non-default agents toward per-agent auth profiles.

options.title: Persist service-managed env values
options.body: Materialize config env through a protected service env file or SecretRef path, accepting the upgrade and credential-storage review burden.

recommendation.title: Keep config-env runtime support
recommendation.body: Confirm config env is supported for managed Gateway turns, add live/systemd proof plus tests, and make `models status` reflect the same runtime context.

likelyOwner.reason: This decision spans config compatibility, service credential storage, docs/status semantics, and setup UX, which matches Peter's recent config/env and policy history.
